name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, 96 GB
arch: x86_64 host + discrete workstation GPU, sm_120
gpu: 96 GB GDDR7, 512-bit; 1792 GB/s (Workstation Edition), 1597 GB/s (Server Edition)
notes: Workstation-class Blackwell with 96 GB GDDR7 — enough to hold a 27B BF16 (51 GB) or a large 4-bit MoE on one card. This is the class the SGLang cookbook targets for a single-GPU Qwen3.8-Flash-Next lane with the PLE table in system RAM.
Two sub-SKUs with different memory bandwidth: Workstation Edition 1792 GB/s, Server Edition 1597 GB/s. A setup must state which board it used; the variant list carries each.
Native FP4/FP8 tensor paths (5th-gen), so NVFP4 checkpoints are architecturally supported. sm_120.
600 W board power (configurable on the Server Edition); MIG up to 4x 24 GB on the Workstation Edition.
Variant ambiguity is real in social posts ('RTX 6000' vs 'RTX PRO 6000'): a recipe naming one must name the edition, or it stays unresolved.

memory.note: dedicated VRAM. Bandwidth differs by edition: Workstation 1792 GB/s, Server 1597 GB/s (each carried on its variant).

compute.note: Workstation Edition: 24,064 CUDA cores, 126 TFLOPS single-precision, 382 RT TFLOPS, 4000 AI TOPS (NVIDIA's theoretical FP4-with-sparsity figure), 600 W. Server Edition: 120 TFLOPS FP32, FP4 tensor 4 PFLOPS, 1597 GB/s. FP16/FP8 dense rates are not published as clean figures, so they stay null.

thermal.note: 600 W total board power; Server Edition is configurable up to 600 W.

variants.name: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition
variants.note: 24,064 CUDA cores; 382 RT TFLOPS; MIG up to 4x 24 GB

variants.name: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
variants.note: 120 TFLOPS FP32, FP4 tensor 4 PFLOPS, FP8 tensor 2 PFLOPS, FP16/BF16 tensor 1 PFLOP

sources.note: Workstation Edition: 4000 AI TOPS, 125 TFLOPS single-precision, 380 RT TFLOPS, 96 GB GDDR7 ECC, 1792 GB/s, 600 W, double flow-through
